findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete after-corpus generation protocol to AC5: specify that the after-corpus is produced by taking the same 40 recorded blobs, applying the A1 transformation (remove baseline_advanced_at from each entry), committing each transformed blob in order into the scratch repo, repacking, and then comparing (pack_after_N – pack_after_1)/(N-1) against the same denominator computed on the before-corpus, with both ratios recorded on the ticket.
evidence: 'The before and after measurements must use the same recorded SHA list and harness; no live Jira access is required.' — yet the after-blobs must differ from the before-blobs (no stamp), so they cannot come from the same SHA list without a specified transformation step.

The remediation describes replaying each revision into 'the same clean scratch-repository harness' and committing it, but only describes the before-corpus construction; the after-corpus construction and the comparison protocol (before-marginal-cost vs. after-marginal-cost) are absent.
'(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)' is given as the formula but it is stated only once; whether this formula applies to the before-corpus, the after-corpus, or their ratio is not disambiguated.
findings.finding: The packed-cost measurement AC requires both a 'before' and an 'after' corpus, but the plan never specifies how the after-A1 blobs are produced. The remediation section says 'the before and after measurements must use the same recorded SHA list and harness,' which is self-contradictory: the whole point is that the after-blobs lack baseline_advanced_at, so they cannot be identical to the historical blobs at those SHAs. The plan does not describe whether the after-corpus is produced by (a) stripping the field from the 40 historical blobs, (b) replaying 40 Jira-state snapshots through the new code, or (c) waiting for 40 real post-A1 commits. Without this specification an executor cannot deterministically construct the after-corpus or know when the measurement AC is satisfied.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria – fifth bullet ('Marginal packed cost per changed version…'); Plan-review remediation section, paragraph beginning 'The packed-cost corpus is the 40 newest…'
scenarios: An executor records the 40 SHAs, implements A1, then is blocked on whether to repack the original blobs (which would show no change from the pre-A1 measurement) or generate new blobs and, if so, by what mechanism.
Without a defined after-corpus the '<=25% of 12.79 KB' threshold cannot be verified in-session, making AC5 unmeasurable.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the ambiguous sentence with: 'Before-corpus: materialize the 40 recorded blobs as-is, commit in SHA order, repack (--window=250 --depth=50), record (pack_40 – pack_1)/39 as the before-marginal. After-corpus: for each blob apply `jq 'del(.. | .baseline_advanced_at? // empty)'` to strip the stamp, commit in the same order into a fresh scratch repo, repack with identical flags, record (pack_40 – pack_1)/39 as the after-marginal. Pass criterion: after-marginal <= 0.25 × before-marginal, with both figures recorded on the ticket.'

findings.finding: The acceptance criteria do not include a test for the first-write / no-existing-baseline boundary case: when `set_baseline` is called for a binding that has no prior baseline entry, the write-when-changed guard must not treat the absent entry as 'equal' to the new baseline and skip the initial write. scenarios: A new Jira ticket is synced for the first time; `set_baseline` is called; the guard compares the new baseline to a missing/empty existing entry and either always writes (correct) or always skips (silent data loss).
